column7: core.RestoreGroup read GetGroupRoles and ran requireGlobalAdminToReinstateAdminRoles, then called storage.RestoreGroup separately and unlocked: a role grant to the still-soft-deleted group landing in that window is invisible to the ceiling check, so a non-global-admin actor's restore passes against a stale (pre-grant) role set and resurrects a group already carrying an admin-conferring role. Reachable because the storage-level write (assignGroupRole, local_rbac.go) never checks the target group's existence or soft-delete state, so a JIT/time-bound grant lands on a soft-deleted group happily. Fixed in #2469 by running the read, the check and the restore write all under sodGrantLockKey("group", id) -- the same key AssignRoleToGroup/AssignGroupRoleWithExpiry already take. Proving test is the pg-gated CROSS-REPLICA one named here, not the SQLite deterministic sibling (TestConcurrency_RestoreGroup_AdminGrantRace_TOCTOU_Deterministic): on SQLite WithNamedLock is an in-process mutex in ONE LocalStorage, so no single-process harness can distinguish a working lock from a deleted Postgres branch -- verified by disabling that branch, which leaves the SQLite test green and turns this one red. FIX-2 also repaired a real vacuity in that SQLite sibling, which passed 3/3 with the WithNamedLock wrapper deleted outright because it paused inside the restore's own write transaction and SQLite's single-writer serialization blocked the racer by itself; its pause moved to WithTransaction entry and it now goes red 3/3 under the same mutation.
